question: Will any of OpenAI’s “Ten Advances in Math and Theoretical CS” be shown to be flawed by the end of August?
resolution_criteria:
[tweet]YES if, by August 31, there is a consensus in credible reporting or within the academic community that at least one of the core arguments or main theorems in OpenAI's "Ten Advances" is fatally flawed or incorrect. Otherwise, resolves NO.

"Flawed" means a core mathematical or theoretical error is identified that invalidates the main result of the paper, and the error is either unfixable or difficult to patch.

Nitpicks—such as minor typos, formatting errors, minor translation gaps in the Lean formalization that do not undermine the mathematical proof's validity, or easily patchable edge cases—do not count toward a YES resolution.

# Research report 1 of 2

I found no evidence, as of 2026-08-16, that any of the ten results has been shown fatally flawed. The one error claim I found says a lemma's printed proof is wrong but the lemma's statement still holds, and it offers its own repair. The other main criticism is about missing credit for prior work, not correctness. My page fetches were all refused by the proxy, so everything below comes from search-result summaries rather than pages I read myself. I left out material dated after 2026-08-16.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no single data source. The question resolves on whether credible reporting or the academic community agrees that a core result is fatally flawed.
- 2026-08-01: OpenAI published "Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science," a 249-page manuscript (one source says the PDF went up July 31). It credits an internal model ("Astra") and comes with Lean 4 certificates in the openai/ten-proofs GitHub repository. [the-decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openai-announces-its-next-major-model-astra-by-dropping-ten-previously-unsolved-math-solutions/), [qz](https://qz.com/openai-astra-model-math-problems-lean-proofs-080326), [forklog](https://forklog.com/en/news/openai-says-internal-astra-model-produced-10-results-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-computer-science)
- One write-up says the formalization reports sorry_count 0 and uses only the standard axioms. Commentators point out this doesn't show the Lean statements match the original open problems, and that community review of that question was still pending. [packetnebula](https://packetnebula.com/articles/openai-astra-ten-lean-proofs/), [mlq.ai](https://mlq.ai/news/openai-publishes-ten-claimed-math-advances-with-formal-peer-review-still-pending/), [s5labs](https://s5labs.io/resources/insights/openai-astra-ten-math-proofs-lean-certificates/)
- None of the results had been through formal journal refereeing. [kingy.ai](https://kingy.ai/news/openai-astra-ten-math-results-evidence/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. I found no consensus, and no strong individual claim, that a main theorem is fatally wrong.
- 2026-08-03: Mikołaj and Krzysztof Sienicki posted an 8-page arXiv note. It says the printed proof of a greedy conditioning lemma in Chapter 6 reverses a condition, and it gives a counterexample to the printed procedure. The authors say the lemma itself is true and offer a corrected proof they call a "local repair." That looks like a patchable issue, not a fatal one. I couldn't open the note itself. [aiunderstanding.org](https://aiunderstanding.org/news/audit-of-an-openai-ai-generated-proof-finds-a-reversed-condition-and-publishes-a-r)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-08-13: Huxiu reports that OpenAI dropped the "at least a decade" wording from its announcement without publishing a list of corrections. [huxiu](https://m.huxiu.com/article/4882806.html)
- 2026-08-12: Commentary pieces about AI and mathematics; none reports a proof error. [mappingignorance](https://mappingignorance.org/2026/08/12/generative-ai-has-changed-mathematics-forever/)
- About 2026-08-06: Scientific American quoted experts calling the release "research misconduct":
  - Steven Miller (Yeshiva University) says the sphere-packing proof reuses his 2016 argument without credit.
  - Francesco Fournier-Facio (Cambridge) says the non-sofic groups result combines ideas from 2016 and 2019 papers.
  - OpenAI says it stands by the results being correct and plans a minor update to fix the citations.
  - These are credit disputes, not claimed errors. [SciAm](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openais-latest-math-breakthroughs-commit-research-misconduct-experts-say/), [aiweekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/openais-astra-math-proofs-draw-research-misconduct-claims), [cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/openai-backlash-math-discovery-astra/)
- 2026-08-03: Max Weinreich's essay "The crisis of AI-generated mathematics" argues against AI in mathematics. It mentions OpenAI's ten solutions but, judging from the abstract, claims no specific error. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.02859), [alphaxiv](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2608.02859)
- 2026-08-03: The Sienicki Chapter 6 lemma note described in section 2.
- Gary Marcus called the model "amazing but vastly oversold." I didn't see a claimed proof error in the summary. [Substack](https://garymarcus.substack.com/p/openais-amazing-but-vastly-oversold)

## 4. Base rates
- I couldn't find a systematic base rate.
- For comparison, earlier high-profile AI math claims (for example the 2025 Erdős-problem episodes) mostly fell apart over prior literature or overclaiming, not over invalid proofs. The early pattern here is the same: credit disputes rather than errors.
- Lean-verified results seldom turn out wrong in the formal sense. The usual way they fail is that the formal statement doesn't match the intended problem, and spotting that tends to take weeks of expert checking.
- The window left is only about 15 days, and the question requires consensus, which usually takes longer than that to form.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold, "Will any of OpenAI's 'Ten Advances…' be shown to be flawed by the end of August?":
  - 2026-08-03 snapshot: about 8%, with 22 traders.
  - Another snapshot shows about 39%, but I couldn't confirm its date or whether it was before 2026-08-16.
  - Commenters there doubted one cited philosophy-paper critique.
  - I couldn't load the page for the current price. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Sketchy/will-any-of-openais-ten-advances-in)
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi market on this.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- OpenAI's promised "minor update" for citations could come out. That would address credit, not correctness.
- The authors or others could respond to the Sienicki Chapter 6 claim. If it's confirmed, it would probably count as patchable, since the authors themselves offer a repair.
- Experts in each field are still checking whether each Lean statement matches the original problem. A mismatch found there is the most plausible route to a "core flaw" claim.
- A further arXiv audit, "A Human Audit of OpenAI's AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs" (arXiv 2608.14673), exists. I couldn't confirm when it was first posted or what it said as of 2026-08-16. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.14673)

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I found no sign, as of Aug 16, of a confirmed error that invalidates any of the ten results. The criticism so far is about credit and novelty, not correctness. Most pages would not load through the proxy, so the dates and details below come from search summaries and are marked as unverified where needed.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no single data series. The question resolves on whether credible reporting or the academic community agrees that a main result is fatally flawed.
- 2026-08-01: OpenAI published "Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science," a 249-page PDF of results from an internal model said to be "Astra." [PDF](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/ten-proofs-oai.pdf), [blog](https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/) (blog page would not load)
- The topics include high-dimensional sphere packing, binary and spherical codes, the first construction of a non-sofic group, a disproof of Connes's rigidity conjecture, arithmetic circuit complexity, quantum parallel repetition, and three Erdős problems. [TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-astra-model-ten-math-proofs-non-sofic-groups), [LessWrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/pQYEPitFqztcRvBsS/openai-s-unreleased-model-astra-solves-ten-major-open)
- The Lean 4 proof files are on GitHub. Secondary reports say they contain zero "sorry" placeholders (Lean's marker for an unproven step). [GitHub](https://github.com/openai/ten-proofs), [s5labs](https://s5labs.io/resources/insights/openai-astra-ten-math-proofs-lean-certificates/)
- The resolver is the Manifold market creator, "Sketchy." [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Sketchy/will-any-of-openais-ten-advances-in)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-08-16: I found no withdrawn result, no OpenAI correction of a theorem, and no expert agreement that any main theorem is wrong.
- Lean checks the logic of each proof. The main remaining way to a YES is a wrong formal statement (the Lean theorem not matching the claimed result) or an error in a result that is not fully formalized. I found no report of either.
- 2026-08 (date unclear): an arXiv preprint, "A Human Audit of OpenAI's AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs" (arXiv:2608.14673), reviewed the results. Its number points to mid-to-late August and it would not load, so I can't confirm its date or findings. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.14673)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Mid-August, dates uncertain: the criticism centers on credit and novelty:
  - Steven Miller (Yeshiva University) says the sphere-packing proof reused an argument from a 2016 paper he co-wrote without credit, and calls it possible "research misconduct." This attacks credit, not correctness. [AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/openais-astra-math-proofs-draw-research-misconduct-claims)
  - Reports say OpenAI quietly reworded its claims that nobody had made progress on these problems for decades. [Kingy](https://kingy.ai/news/openai-astra-ten-math-results-evidence/)
- Early to mid-August: independent mathematicians began checking the Lean files line by line. [Startup Fortune](https://startupfortune.com/independent-mathematicians-are-now-lean-checking-openais-proof-claims-line-by-line/)
  - One reviewer reported a sign ("polarity") error in Chapter 6, the quantum parallel repetition result. Coverage dated after Aug 16 should not be used here, so the outcome of that claim isn't covered.
- Early August: Thomas Bloom, who reviewed the work, called it "big news." Others pointed out that none of it has been peer reviewed and that credit is unclear. [Datafloq](https://datafloq.com/openai-solved-ten-open-math-problems-nobody-can-say-who-gets-credit/), [DataCamp](https://www.datacamp.com/blog/open-ai-model-astra-solved-ten-open-math-problems)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no formal base rate.
- Past AI math claims have mostly failed on novelty, not correctness. In October 2025, OpenAI's claims that GPT-5 had solved Erdős problems were walked back because the solutions already existed in the literature; the proofs themselves were not wrong. That is from memory, I did not check it here.
- Results that are fully checked in Lean, with no "sorry," are rarely shown to be fatally wrong within weeks. Problems that do appear are usually a formal statement that doesn't match the claim. Human-written major claims get serious errors found more often (for example the 2023 LK-99 superconductor claim and some claimed P vs NP proofs), but those had no formal checking.
- The window is only about 15 days, and real expert agreement on a fatal flaw usually takes longer to form.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold, this question: 39% YES in a snapshot of unknown date. The market's definition of "flawed" matches the one given here. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Sketchy/will-any-of-openais-ten-advances-in)
- Manifold, a related market covering the GitHub repo with a November 30 deadline: about 34% YES (snapshot). [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Sketchy/will-any-of-openais-massive-release)
- I found nothing on Polymarket or Kalshi.

## 6. Upcoming events before Aug 31
- Final or revised versions of the arXiv human audit (2608.14673), including how the Chapter 6 sign-error claim turns out.
- More independent Lean audits, especially comparing the formal statements with the claims in the paper.
- Expert write-ups and any OpenAI errata or reworded claims on its blog or GitHub.
- Further coverage of the Miller credit dispute. On its own this should not count toward YES, since it concerns attribution rather than correctness.

clusion.
- About 2026-08-06: the Scientific American criticism (Miller, Fournier-Facio) is about credit and novelty, not correctness, and OpenAI stands by the results.
- Thomas Bloom reviewed the work and called it "big news."
- The Lean certificates reportedly have zero sorry and use only standard axioms.
- The Manifold snapshot from 2026-08-03 was about 8%, and a related market with a November 30 deadline sits at about 34%, which suggests the 39% figure is noisy or thinly traded.
- Fifteen days is short for a consensus to form.

**(e) Scenarios**
- No: audits keep turning up citation gaps, local proof slips with repairs, and some debate over statement fidelity. OpenAI issues a minor update, and no main theorem is agreed to be false by August 31.
- Yes: an audit shows that one Lean statement materially differs from the claimed open problem, or that a non-formalized step fails. Experts quickly agree, OpenAI retracts or downgrades that result, and the creator resolves Yes.

**(f) From base rate to final**
I start at about 7%. I adjust up slightly for the active audits, ten independent chances for a statement mismatch, the unknown content of the second audit, and the unexplained 39% snapshot. I adjust down for the consensus requirement, the short window, and the fact that the only concrete error claim comes with its own repair. I do not anchor on the Manifold price because it is thin, undated and inconsistent with the related market. That leaves me at about 9%.

Probability: 9%
